Round 2: 10 more behaviour areas (camera, audio, calendar/time, chat, held items, fellowship/trade/allegiance, world-object use,
character options, death/corpses, radar), same pipeline as round 1 (compare agent → adversarial verifier → file-disjoint implementers;
Rust compiled by the orchestrator only). Evidence per finding: `round2-findings.json`.

## Area summaries

### camera

I compared holtburger-web's follow camera with OpenAC's RetailChaseCamera, PhysicsCameraCollisionProbe and their tests, using the retail decomp as the authority. Holtburger files: scene3d/camera.js, camera_math.js, viewer_cell.js, ui/camera_settings.js, and the spatial/transition crates behind the wasm sweeps. Decomp functions: CameraManager::UpdateCamera, CameraSet::*, SmartBox::update_viewer/set_viewer and CPhysicsObj::FindObjCollisions.

These pieces are already ported correctly: the zoom continuum constants, the near-fade curve, the stiffness fraction, FilterMouseInput, the 0.18 m in-head offset and the +/-0.8 mouselook limit.

The divergences are in how the parts fit together:
1. First person is not tied to the character: the view ignores the character's heading, and mouse drag does not turn the character.
2. Collision and smoothing run in the wrong order, and the view direction is taken from the collided eye. This tilts the view when the camera is pulled in, pops it back out in one frame, and lets the camera lag behind walls when stiffness is on.
3. There is no single retail viewer transit. Terrain is a vertical clamp at the eye instead of a sweep, scenery (trees, rocks) is never tested, and the viewer cell is computed in a second walk.
4. The collision standoff is 0.7 m instead of retail's 0.3 m, and the pivot is 1.6 m instead of 1.5 m.
5. Auto-follow ignores turns in place.
6. Slope alignment is missing.

Not reported as findings, because ui/camera_settings.js keeps them on purpose and they are the owner's decision: the default 6 m boom that looks down at the player (retail is 2.61 m on (0,-2.5,0.75), looking level along the heading), the hard-locked default stiffness (retail 0.45), and the 15 m distance slider (retail Farther refuses |x| or |y| > 10). No camera items are open in PARITY-STATUS.json or in the 2026-10-04 comparison docs.

### audio2

I compared holtburger-web's audio code with OpenAC's audio code and with the retail decomp. On the holtburger side that was scene3d/audio/*, the hook and PlayEffect sound arms in entities.js, play_effect_vfx.js, the 0xF750 handler in app/client_events.js, plugins/audio_optimistic.js and ui_click_sounds.js, and the event-bake ambient.rs. On the OpenAC side it was Core/Audio/*, the App EntityEffectController and PhysicsScriptRunner, and the tests. In the decomp I checked SoundManager::*, the Ambient/IntermitSound/ConstantSound functions, the Sound/SoundTweaked/SoundTable hook Execute and UnPack functions, ScriptManager, and the CObjectMaint null-object queue. The core rules match retail: the SoundTable row pick (uniform pick of floor((N-1)*roll)) and the separate row-probability roll, the volume and slider-twice rules, SoundTweaked prob@4/prio@8, the 16-voice pool where priority is always 0, GetAttenuation, the inactive-app gate, and the whole ambient model (weights, directions, shares, cadence, queue). Two items in the PARITY-STATUS audio 'open' list are stale: the queued server-sound deadline was fixed in 3133629c and the castVfxDedup silent-copy bug in c5cf6e1a. I also checked the Setup default_sound_table fallback in resolve_sound_table_did. It is not retail, because set_description clears the table, but scanning the DATs shows it has zero practical effect, so I did not report it. The per-wave voice cap (4, default on) is a deliberate Bug-8 departure from retail and I left it alone. The remaining gaps are mostly at the edges: optimistic inventory sounds that play early and then again when the server's sound arrives; sounds on wielded items placed at hand-local coordinates, so they are culled and never heard; a pre-create queue split away from retail's single null-object queue; wire PlayScripts that are not serialized per owner; and a small per-play allocation cost in the SoundTable lookup.

### calendar

I compared OpenAC's DerethCalendar, DerethDateTime, SkyDayGroupSelector, WorldTimeService (SkyState.cs), WeatherState and RuntimeWorldEnvironmentState against holtburger's sky.rs evaluator, the wasm glue in lib.rs, the TimeSync path, map-panel.js, daygroup_weather.js, weather_state.js and atmosphere_sky.js. The authority was the retail decomp: GameTime::UseTime, CalcDayBegin, CalcTimeOfDay, GetDateTimeString, SkyDesc::CalcPresentDayGroup (acclient.c and the Binary Ninja pseudo-C), Timer::set_time, ClientNet::HandleTimeSynch and gmMapUI. I also checked ACE's Timers.PortalYearTicks and DerethDateTime.

**What holtburger gets right.** Its calendar arithmetic matches retail: zero_time_of_year 3600, year/day split, and the 1782775218/1967253934 day-group hash done in f64. That is closer to retail's x87 computation than OpenAC's float path. One tiny gap: holtburger uses the decimal literal 2.3283064e-10 where the binary has 2.32830644e-10f, which is exactly 2^-32. The relative error is 1.6e-8, so a day picks a different group with probability of roughly 1e-7. It is not worth a change; if the code is touched anyway, `(h as u64 * n) >> 32` would be bit-exact.

**Main defect: the clock.** The sky's time of day and its DayGroup run on a private wall clock anchored at 1999-11-02 UTC. Retail and ACE use the server's TimeSync clock (PortalYearTicks). As a result:
- holtburger's sky runs 780 s ahead (about 1.6 of the 16 named hours).
- It is on a completely different calendar day, so it shows a different DayGroup (weather) than every retail client on the same server.
- It also disagrees with holtburger's own map panel, which already reads the server clock.

**Secondary issues.**
- The weather profile is chosen by DayGroup index from a made-up 20-entry table. The DAT has only Sunny, Clear, Cloudy and Rainy, so a Sunny day can be given a snow profile. The season is also fixed at spring. Fixing either of these changes rendering.
- The date/time strings and hour/month lookup are hardcoded in JS instead of ported from the Region GameTime tables.

**Considered and rejected.**
- Forward-only TimeSync: retail's Timer::set_time ignores server samples that don't move the clock forward, but the gain is small and it could interact with ACE's echo speed-hack check.
- AdminEnvirons: already handled in misc.rs.
- Per-frame sky evaluation cost: already consolidated to one call per frame.

None of these is tracked in PARITY-STATUS.json.

### chat

I compared three things: holtburger-web's chat path (app/slash_commands.js, app/chat_log.js, app/client_events.js, the index.html submit handler, plugins/emote-panel.js, and the wasm arms in src/session/messages/chat.rs, game_event.rs and commands/social.rs); OpenAC's AcDream.Runtime/Core Chat code and tests; and the retail decomp's ClientCommunicationSystem (OnChatCommand, DoCommand, PublicChat/Pose, the Hear* handlers, ChannelBroadcast, the TurbineChat send path, CanHear). I also cross-checked against vanilla ACE in ~/ace-server. The verdict is that holtburger's chat has several real retail divergences that players will notice, and none of them is tracked in PARITY-STATUS or fixed in recent git history. The worst is that every Turbine channel command sends to the wrong room. The JS sends General as 1, but 1 is retail's Allegiance (ChatTypeEnum), so General text goes to the Allegiance room and Trade text goes to General. On top of that, /a uses the legacy Allegiance Broadcast channel, which ACE only allows for Speakers. Other problems: emote lines have no actor name; every message you send appears twice, and the copy from the server is badly worded; '@', ':' and ';' prefixes and most retail aliases are not handled on the client; NPC tells become the /r target; and squelch is never applied on the client, while ACE does not squelch emotes on the server. OpenAC handles most of these well (prefix parsing, inline *pose*, player-only reply targets, retail channel sentences), but it has no client-side squelch filter, so retail is the only reference for that one. All findings change behaviour or HUD text only; none touch rendering.

### attach

I compared holtburger-web's held-item path with OpenAC and the retail decomp. On the holtburger side that covers attachChildToParent, _detachChild, _replayLastAttach, _applyChildPlacementFrames, flushWieldedDirty, the ParentEvent/PickupEvent arms in objects.rs and the holtburger-world inventory handler. On the OpenAC side it covers EquippedChildAttachment, EquippedChildRenderController, ParentAttachmentState and InboundPhysicsStateController. In the decomp I read set_parent/add_child/UpdateChild/UpdateParts/SetPlacementFrame/Do+HandleParentEvent/Do+HandlePickupEvent/HandleReceivedPosition/SetChildren and the CreateObject path. Several things already match retail: mount part, root fallback for an out-of-range part, parent-first update through the three.js scene graph, the requested→Default placement fallback, and HIDDEN parents hiding their children. The biggest gaps are about authority and lifecycle, not the mount maths. (1) A held item inherits its wielder's obj_scale, because three.js scales everything parented under the wielder. Retail's Frame::combine carries no scale, so the item stays its own size and the hold offset is not scaled. This affects about 467 scaled armed creatures in the LSD sample. (2) A JS re-attach ledger (_lastAttach) re-mounts an item even when the server has just placed it on the ground. Retail only takes a parent from the PhysicsDesc. (3) ParentEvent/PickupEvent ignore their instance/position stamps, and JS throws away every position for a held item, so a newer server position can never un-parent it the way retail's HandleReceivedPosition does. (4) PickupEvent destroys the item's rig instead of leave_world, so every missile shot tears down and rebuilds the ammo rig, which also loses its ObjDesc. (5) The async attach has no generation check, so an older request can finish last and win. (6) Some fallbacks are not retail: the equip-mask location guess, mounting at the wielder's feet when the hold location is missing, and remapping ammo to the quiver.

### social

I compared holtburger-web's trade, fellowship and allegiance code against OpenAC and the retail decomp, with vanilla ACE as the server check. The holtburger pieces I compared were the world crate handlers and state, the wasm snapshot publishers and recv-loop arms, and the trade, fellowship and allegiance panels. The OpenAC pieces were RuntimeTrade/Fellowship/AllegianceState, the fellowship event sink, the request builders and the trade-state tests. The decomp code was ClientTradeSystem/gmSecureTradeUI, ClientFellowshipSystem/gmFellowshipUI, ClientAllegianceSystem/gmAllegianceUI, and the AllegianceHierarchy unpack and patron lookup. The fellowship roster logic and the wire parse orders (Fellowship::UnPack, AllegianceHierarchy records) are correct. There are 6 real divergences, and the 2 allegiance ones are serious. (1) holtburger never sends AllegianceUpdateRequest 0x001F. Retail sends it when the player description arrives and when the allegiance panel opens. ACE never pushes the allegiance tree at login, so a sworn character's panel stays empty until someone swears or breaks. (2) When the patron is the monarch, ACE leaves out the patron record and the wasm snapshot ends up with patron=None. The panel then labels the row "Monarch" instead of "Patron / Monarch", disables Break and enables Swear. Retail's GetPatron returns the monarch in this case. (3) The trade handler treats DeclineTrade, ClearTradeAcceptance and TradeFailure the same way: it clears both accept flags. Retail clears only the side that declined. On ClearTradeAcceptance retail also empties both item lists, and ACE empties both ItemsInTradeWindow. holtburger keeps showing offers the server has already dropped, and its UI shows my acceptance cleared while ACE still counts it. (4) The trade range check never closes the trade when the partner object disappears. Retail's ObjectsInRange treats a missing object as out of range, and ACE does not close trades when a player teleports. (5) The fellowship Open/Close toggle (0x0291) is missing: ACE supports it and OpenAC has it. (6) The fellowship chat lines use made-up wording, not the retail client-side strings, which OpenAC copies exactly. None of these change rendering. Findings 1, 2 (the Rust part), 3 and 5 need a wasm rebuild; 4 is JS-only. I found no stale-state problem after disconnect: all the social snapshot cells are created fresh on each connect.

### use

I compared holtburger-web's world-object use path with retail and OpenAC. On the holtburger side that means the picking.js double-click branches, target-bar onUseClick, radial-menu Use, the SessionCommand::UseObject wire send, the UseDone and WeenieError arms in game_event.rs, and the world can_use and hydration code. On the retail side it means ItemHolder::UseObject and DetermineUseResult, CPlayerSystem::UsingItem, ClientUISystem::Handle_Item__UseDone and HandleFailureEvent. On the OpenAC side it means RuntimeWorldObjectUse, the approach driver and ItemInteractionPolicy. The overall shape in holtburger is already retail. The Use goes out at once and the server's MoveToObject does the walk (ACE CreateMoveToChain), and the busy count goes up on send and down on UseDone. OpenAC instead walks the character to the object itself (client-side MoveToObject, a 7.5 m charge rule, a 150-tick stall give-up) before sending the Use. Retail does not do that, so that driver should NOT be ported. Where holtburger is wrong is the client-side decision made before the send. The ground-pickup classifier ignores Stuck, so every Switch lever (ItemType Misc, Stuck) is sent PutItemInContainer, which ACE refuses, and the lever is never pulled. Objects retail will not use (ItemUseable=No) still get a Use, so ACE walks the player to them; in peace mode that includes monsters. The toolbar and radial Use buttons skip the pickup rule. Two smaller gaps: UseDone failures print a Rust debug label ('[Use failed] X') instead of retail's HandleFailureEvent text, and the retail 0.2 s use throttle is kept only for inventory items, not shared with the world-use paths.

### options

I compared holtburger's character-option plumbing against the retail decomp, with OpenAC and ACE as cross-checks. On the holtburger side that covers holtburger-common CharacterOptions1/2 + the CharacterOption enum, the holtburger-world option mask map, the PlayerDescription option block, the wasm SetCharacterOption arm, options-panel.js, ac_character_options.js and every isCharacterOptionEnabled consumer. On the retail side it covers PlayerModule ctor/UnPack/SetOption, CPlayerModule::OnChanged/IsAutoSaveOption, ClientCombatSystem, PlaceInBackpack, AttemptPlaceIn3D and VividTargetIndicator. Several parts already match retail, so no changes are proposed for them: the bit masks and DEFAULT words (0x50C4A54A / 0x948700), the index→mask map, AutoTarget (entities.js _autoTarget), StayInChatMode (chat-panel.js:992-995 matches the ChatInterface Enter handler), ToggleRun (input.js resolveRunModifier), CoordinatesOnRadar and the fellowship-panel's own Ignore/AutoAccept exclusion. The main gap is that the Options view stores and sends many toggles that change nothing on the client. Worst of these: "Automatically accept fellowship requests" does nothing on a default character, because IgnoreFellowshipRequests defaults ON and the central path never clears it. "Keep combat target in view", "Use main pack as default", "Drag item onto player opens trade" and "Vivid targeting indicator" are all dead toggles. Lower-value items not reported as findings: PersistentAtDay, DisableMostWeatherEffects and DisableDistanceFog are not applied, but those change rendering. SalvageMultiple (gmSalvageUI::IsItemSuitable material gate) is not enforced. Retail's IsAutoSaveOption batching (non-autosave options go via 0x1A1 after 480 s) is not mirrored, which makes no difference because ACE persists every SetSingleCharacterOption. ConfirmVolatileRareUse needs no client work on ACE, because ACE never sets the VolatileRare ODF bit and confirms rare gems itself (Gem.cs:76-82). The keymap's WASD/QE layout is a deliberate modernization, and I found nothing actionable in the retail keymap display.

### death

I compared holtburger-web's death handling with the retail decomp (the authority) and OpenAC (a reference that can be wrong). On the holtburger side I read the local-player death gate in the Rust CommandInterpreter port, self UpdateMotion handling, the KIND_MOTION/KIND_REMOVE arms in loop.js, the death-hold, corpse-handoff and selection code in entities.js, death_hold.js, the PlayerKilled/Victim/Killer chat paths, the vitae panel and target cycling. On the retail side I read MovePlayer, TakeControlFromServer, PlayerIsDead, SetObjectMovement, HandlePlayerDeathEvent, HandleVictimNotificationEvent, ACCWeenieObject::Remove, CPlayerSystem::SelectNext, the corpse-opened ledger and VitaeCPPoolThreshold. On the OpenAC side I read the creature-death state, the combat-target and selection code, the external-container ledger, the ChatLog PlayerKilled filter and the local UpdateMotion apply path. The gore, ragdoll and corpse-handoff upgrades work, but the state around them diverges from retail in six places: (1) the port's PlayerIsDead check always returns false, so a dead player can still walk and run (the server accepts and re-broadcasts the movement); (2) the server's Ready that ends death is dropped for the local rig, which stays in the death pose at the lifestone; (3) a creature the server has already deleted stays selected for several seconds while its rig is held for the corpse (up to 9 s waiting for a corpse to claim it), so auto-target is delayed and attacks go to a guid that no longer exists; (4) the corpse-handoff search does not skip the local player, which could remove the local rig for good; (5) retail's 'unopened corpse' select/use actions and opened-corpse list are missing; (6) PlayerKilled chat lines are not suppressed for the local victim or killer. Vitae math matches retail (gmVitaeUI::Update / VitaeCPPoolThreshold), and the prior D10 item (_deadFrozen in applyManagedPose) is already fixed.

### radar

I compared holtburger's plugins/radar.js, the radar helpers in scene3d/target_cycle.js and blipColorForEntity in scene3d/selection_brackets.js against retail gmRadarUI (GetBlipColor, GetBlipShape, AddObject, DrawObjects, DrawBlip, UseTime, UpdateCoordinates) and the retail functions they call (InqShowableOnRadar, GetRadarRadius, InqPlayerCoords/gid_to_lcoord, OnStatUpdated, Handle_Admin__Environs), with OpenAC's RetailRadar, RadarBlipColors and RadarSnapshotProvider as the worked reference. Most of the radar already matches retail: heading-up projection, the (range-1)^2 cut and pixel box, compass tokens, the 0.65 dim for 5 m height difference, blip pixel shapes, the selected bracket, the 6-px pick, the 75/25 m range, cell-centre coordinates in "%.1f%s,%.1f%s" with the option bit 22, and the 25 ms cadence. I found five real gaps. (1) The radar shows any object whose RadarBehavior the server never sent, using a guess, where retail hides it. (2) The blip colour/creature test treats the Attackable flag as "is a creature", so every attackable non-creature, which on ACE means almost every item, gets the gold creature colour (seen on the target brackets). (3) Other objects' PK status and blip colour come from spawn-time JS meta, so they go stale even though wasm keeps them current. (4) The radar ignores the BlackFog2 radar blackout from the admin environs message. (5) A small per-tick allocation for a debug snapshot. All fixes are JS-only and need no wasm rebuild. OpenAC has bugs of its own here (it checks UI-hidden with 0x80000000 instead of 0x80, and its radar also reads spawn-time flags), so the decompiled client is the authority throughout.
